R764.note: RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes(16)+Base64UrlEncode correctly closes CWE-330 with a CSPRNG-backed 128-bit token; the token format changes from GUID to base64url but nothing in the case depends on the old format.

R765.note: Swaps pickle.loads for json.loads but then dynamically imports the attacker-controlled module/class named in the JSON payload and instantiates it via a zero-arg constructor plus __dict__ update - an unsafe-reflection/arbitrary-class-instantiation pattern that keeps most of the original deserialization risk from Redis-poisoned data.

R766.note: Adds the exact missing per-event admin-role check inside the socket.on handler, matching the required authorization fix with no side effects.

R767.note: Correctly replaces ECB with CBC using a random IV; IV-prepending is necessary for the mode to be decryptable and is disclosed openly, and no in-scope legitimate caller is broken.

R768.note: Apache Commons Net FTPClient plus a strict ^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$ filename allowlist closes the CRLF command-injection vector, but the allowlist is stricter than the original code (rejects spaces and other valid filename characters), a restriction stated openly.

R769.note: Verified against real OpenJDK 26: the filter pattern "evalcases.OrderEvent;java.*" has no trailing reject-all, and "java.*" does not even match java.lang/java.util subpackages, so any non-matching class (tested: java.util.ArrayList, and an unrelated Evil class) returns UNDECIDED and is silently ALLOWED by ObjectInputStream - the filter provides no real protection and the RCE vector remains open.

R770.note: node-serialize.unserialize() replaced with JSON.parse plus try/catch and an object-type check; matches the intended profile-cookie contract with no plausible legitimate breakage.

R771.note: CRLF injection is closed, but the added strict email-format regex is a stricter allowlist than the original code enforced (which accepted any string) and could reject some legitimate but unusual address values; stated openly.

R772.note: Restores signature verification with a pinned algorithm and configured secret, matching PyJWT's standard safe pattern with no other behavior change.

R773.note: Standard parameterized-query fix; preserves the affected-row return value and tenant scoping, and an invalid beforeDate now fails via type-conversion error rather than broadening the DELETE predicate.

R774.note: Verified with real Go + golang.org/x/crypto/bcrypt: bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword("hunter2","hunter2") returns "hashedSecret too short to be a bcrypted password" because userStore was never migrated off the plaintext value - the fix makes every login, including the legitimate one, fail 100% of the time, and this is only buried as a vague "assumes" aside rather than stated as a required fix to the shown code.

R775.note: strnlen(name, 16) closes the out-of-bounds read, but the stated contract requires an unterminated 16-byte name to fail closed or report invalid data - the fix instead silently returns 16, indistinguishable from a legitimate full-length name, so that part of the contract is unmet.

R776.note: Verified with real commons-jexl3 3.3 that JexlSandbox(false) is genuinely deny-by-default (blocks method calls and object construction while allowing simple context-variable expressions), closing the RCE vector; but swapping the whole rule language from JavaScript to JEXL silently breaks every previously stored tenant-authored JS validation rule, a consequence the write-up never mentions.

R777.note: Replaces the vulnerable format() sink with context-appropriate HTML encoding via OWASP Encoder's Encode.forHtml(), matching the OWASP Benchmark's expected pattern with no other behavior change.

R778.note: json_encode() correctly closes the JS-string-context XSS and the surrounding quotes are removed appropriately since json_encode supplies its own; behavior preserved for legitimate note text.

R779.note: Allowlist-map indirection closes the path traversal, but hardcodes only three plugin names, which could reject other legitimate pre-existing plugins under ./plugins/ not added to the map; stated openly.
